newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine judge suspends telecom rate rises.
newsitem.headline: Argentine judge suspends telecom rate rises.

text.p: An Argentine judge Thursday suspended recent increases in local telephone rates after a court action presented by a consumer group, the legal representative of Free Consumers said.
"As of today the new tariffs are no longer applied," said Socialist Party congressman Hector Polino, who is also Free Consumers' legal representive.

Polino told local television that Judge Liliana Maria Cegeilan had accepted the group's request to put the rate rises on hold until the courts ruled on the legality of a decree authorizing the tariff changes.
But Polino said the ruling did not reverse cuts in domestic and international long-distance rates.
The judge's decision is the latest in a volley of court rulings on the tariff changes, which have become a legal football since authorized by decree late in January.

A federal judge last week suspended the new tariff structure pending a ruling brought by the nation's Ombudsman on a court case to have the tariff changes reversed. But the tariffs came back into force Wednesday after the government presented an appeal.
The changes increased the cost of local calls and telephone rentals but slashed the rates for national and international long distance calls.

Telefonica de Argentina and Telecom Argentina had waged a long lobbying campaign for the tariff changes, which they said would make charges fairer for provincial businesses. They also hoped it would make them more competitive when the Argentine phone market is thrown open to all competition, probably in the year 2000.

But consumer groups and opposition parties fought hard against the charges and argued in public hearings ending in December 1996 that private users' telephone bills would rise and the phone companies pocket the difference.
The companies argued the new charges would not increase their profits. Telefonica is controlled by Telefonica de Espana, and Telecom by France Telecom.
